scope: Primary-source bibliographic metadata and relevant findings for the cited factor-timing literature

papers.title: Time-Series Variation in Factor Premia: The Influence of the Business Cycle
papers.reference: Polk, C., Haghbin, M., & de Longis, A. (2020). Time-series variation in factor premia: The influence of the business cycle. Journal of Investment Management, 18(1), 69–89. https://personal.lse.ac.uk/polk/research/PolkHaghbinDeLongis2020.pdf

primary_sources.verified: Title, authors, year, volume, issue, pages and abstract

papers.scoped_finding: Their business-cycle classification combines leading economic indicators and global risk appetite to rotate among size, value, quality, low volatility and momentum. The published abstract reports information ratios nearly 70% above a static multifactor allocation after accounting for transaction costs and other implementation considerations.
papers.avoid_claim: The present report neither replicates nor disproves the approximately 70% information-ratio result. RMW is an operating-profitability spread and is not identical to their quality exposure.

papers.title: Optimal Timing and Tilting of Equity Factors
papers.reference: Dichtl, H., Drobetz, W., Lohre, H., Rother, C., & Vosskamp, P. (2019). Optimal timing and tilting of equity factors. Financial Analysts Journal, 75(4), 84–102. https://doi.org/10.1080/0015198X.2019.1645478

primary_sources.verified: Full bibliographic metadata, DOI and abstract

papers.scoped_finding: Using parametric portfolio policies for global equity factors, they find predictive relations with fundamental and technical signals but limited ability to profit from them after transaction costs; smoothing turnover improves timing evidence only modestly.
papers.avoid_claim: Do not say transaction costs explain the present report's null finding if gross allocation gains are already statistically uncertain.

papers.title: The Promises and Pitfalls of Factor Timing
papers.reference: Bender, J., Sun, X., Thomas, R., & Zdorovtsov, V. (2018). The promises and pitfalls of factor timing. The Journal of Portfolio Management, 44(4), 79–92. https://doi.org/10.3905/jpm.2018.44.4.079

primary_sources.verified: Authors, title, journal, year, volume, issue, pages and DOI hyperlink

primary_sources.type: Author paper presented via Wharton Jacobs Levy Center
primary_sources.verified: April 2017 working-paper abstract and discussion underlying the 2018 published article

papers.scoped_finding: The authors examine sentiment, valuation, trend, economic and financial-condition predictors, stressing that relevance depends on the investment horizon and that changing relationships and hindsight can undermine factor timing.
papers.avoid_claim: Do not portray this as evidence of an identical monthly US five-factor implementation or a universally successful timing method.

papers.title: Forecasting the Equity Risk Premium: The Role of Technical Indicators
papers.reference: Neely, C. J., Rapach, D. E., Tu, J., & Zhou, G. (2014). Forecasting the equity risk premium: The role of technical indicators. Management Science, 60(7), 1772–1791. https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2013.1838

primary_sources.verified: Full bibliographic metadata, DOI and abstract

papers.scoped_finding: For the aggregate US equity premium, technical and macroeconomic indicators contain complementary information across the business cycle, and combining them improves forecasts compared with either information set alone in their design.
papers.avoid_claim: This is an aggregate-market forecasting result, not evidence that the same gains transfer to five long-short equity factors.

papers.title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
papers.reference: Moreira, A., & Muir, T. (2017). Volatility-managed portfolios. The Journal of Finance, 72(4), 1611–1644. https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.12513

primary_sources.verified: Full bibliographic metadata, DOI and abstract

papers.scoped_finding: Reducing risk when lagged volatility is high improves risk-adjusted performance for several factors in their analysis because conditional expected returns do not rise proportionately with volatility.
papers.avoid_claim: The report's capped, shrunk forecast-over-variance mapping is not a replication of the paper's inverse-variance timing strategy. Gains shared by macro and historical-mean allocations do not identify an incremental macro effect.

papers.title: The Virtue of Complexity in Return Prediction
papers.reference: Kelly, B., Malamud, S., & Zhou, K. (2024). The virtue of complexity in return prediction. The Journal of Finance, 79(1), 459–503. https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.13298

primary_sources.verified: Full bibliographic metadata, DOI, theory scope and aggregate US market application

papers.scoped_finding: In their theoretical setting and aggregate US market application, richly parameterized nonlinear feature models can improve out-of-sample market-timing performance. They also show that forecast R-squared can be an incomplete guide to portfolio value.
papers.avoid_claim: Do not infer that a selected Ridge penalty at the upper grid boundary proves macro information is absent, or that arbitrarily adding predictors must improve this report's factor allocation. Their paper explicitly distinguishes raw signals from nonlinear model complexity.
